clue.text: Possibly transposing a Beethoven work for violin and piano

definitions.text: Beethoven work for violin and piano

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the following words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A musician wonders about shifting a Beethoven violin sonata into another key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transposing' looks like a musical instruction but, with 'a', it is the anagram fodder; 'Possibly' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Violin Sonata No 5 in F is known by this nickname, a piece for violin with piano.

clue.text: Diocese with best china, that's apparent

parts.note: a see is the area a bishop governs, a diocese
Ming porcelain from China is the finest and most prized

explanation.surface: A bishop's palace displays its finest porcelain for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seeming is outwardly so, evident on the surface though perhaps not in truth.

clue.text: Recite something taken from computer memory

definitions.meaning: to recite is to speak a text aloud to listeners
a display or printout of data a computer has stored

explanation.definitionFit: To deliver written words to an audience is one sense; a display of stored data is the other.

clue.text: Flower, exotic, Russians cultivated initially

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so these letters are made strange by rearranging
initially picks out the opening letter of the word cultivated

explanation.surface: Some Russian gardeners grew an unusual foreign bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' shuffles RUSSIANS together with C, the first letter of 'cultivated' as 'initially' says.
explanation.definitionFit: This daffodil genus is a spring bulb grown for its white or yellow blooms.

clue.text: Greek philosopher resigned

definitions.meaning: a follower of Zeno's school in ancient Athens

explanation.definitionFit: Zeno's school taught calm endurance, so its name also describes patient acceptance of misfortune.

clue.text: Painter more dapper in appearance

explanation.definitionFit: A French rococo portraitist shares his surname with the comparative of an adjective for smartly dressed.

clue.text: Fast stream in high hill fissure

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor
a rent is a split or tear

explanation.surface: Water rushes down through a crack in a craggy hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: A rushing mountain flow of water, violent and swift, is the synonym.

clue.text: This butter is high

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'This butter is high' with no count, and answer held as MOUNTAINGOA, cut short of MOUNTAIN GOAT (a high butter, cryptic definition); the stored answer is truncated.

clue.text: Old swan song for the outdoors

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: An ageing swan sings its final song out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swan song' reads as one phrase meaning a farewell performance, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out under the sky, not indoors, is the sense of this phrase.

clue.text: Emergence of unfashionable vintage

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
a vintage is a year's crop of grapes

explanation.surface: A wine-lover notes the arrival of a year's wine that has gone out of style.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock breaking through the surface of the ground is a geological emergence.

clue.text: Fit to crack up?

parts.note: seems to ask about someone ready to break down in laughter, but crack up means to praise highly

explanation.definitionFit: To crack something up is to praise it, so something deserving of acclaim is fit for it.

clue.text: A robin, one hopping about in capital

indicators.note: a bird hopping about moves its position, so the letters move around

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A robin and another bird hop around a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hopping about' rearranges A ROBIN; the I from 'one' goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Kenya.

clue.text: Wild notion to ring painter

parts.note: to chime is to ring like a bell
RA, Royal Academician, a crossword painter

explanation.surface: Someone has a crazy idea of telephoning an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanciful, impossible idea is a figurative sense of the mythical monster.

clue.text: Proceed in mastery of slang?

indicators.note: in places the word for proceed within the word for mastery

parts.note: art is skill or mastery
to go is to proceed

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to move on to becoming expert in street talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A group's private jargon or cant is a form of slang.

clue.text: Drenches with tears at US assembly

indicators.note: an assembly puts parts together, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: An audience in America is soaked by crying.
explanation.definitionFit: To soak something until it holds no more liquid is the synonym.

clue.text: Trial marriage held at Sabina Park, possibly

parts.note: a test is a trial
a match is a marriage, as in a good match

explanation.surface: A couple try living together before a wedding in a Jamaican park.
explanation.walkthrough: Sabina Park is a cricket ground in Kingston, Jamaica, which hosts international matches between national cricket teams.
explanation.definitionFit: An international cricket fixture is the kind of game staged at this ground, hence possibly.

clue.text: Half-month schedules for London and Wells, for example

indicators.note: half asks for the first four of the word for a month's eight letters

parts.note: November is a month
lists are schedules

explanation.surface: Fortnightly timetables cover the cities of London and Wells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-month' suggests a fortnight but gives NOVE, half of November; Jack London and H G Wells are writers, not cities.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack London and H G Wells both wrote fiction, so they are examples of story writers.

clue.text: English resort opening with no road to it?

parts.note: a vent is an opening
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A seaside town is reached only through a gap without any road.
explanation.walkthrough: VENTNOR is a seaside resort on the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This Isle of Wight town is a seaside holiday destination.

clue.text: Such meteors in showers end soil cultivation

indicators.note: cultivating soil turns it over, so these letters are turned over into a new order

explanation.surface: Rain showers bring an end to farming the land.
explanation.definitionFit: These November meteors, appearing to come from Leo, arrive in annual showers.

clue.text: Neat bend in this stock collar

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, of which an ox is one
to bow is to bend

explanation.surface: A tidy curve is put in a farmer's livestock harness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy but is the old word for cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped wooden collar fitted round an ox's neck is for livestock.

clue.text: Bunting flying in Oporto lanes

indicators.note: in says the bird sits inside the run of letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A small bird flits through the streets of a Portuguese city.
explanation.definitionFit: This small European songbird is a kind of bunting, once eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Rotten day in Rome for western villains

parts.note: bad means rotten
dies is the Latin word for day

explanation.surface: A dreadful day in Rome is spent watching cowboy film baddies.
explanation.walkthrough: DIES is Latin for day, hence 'in Rome'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad guys in cowboy films are the informal term for villains.

clue.text: Have target that works to scorer's disadvantage

parts.note: to own is to have
a goal is a target

explanation.surface: Having an aim can sometimes backfire on whoever scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting the ball into your own net gives points to the opponents, against the player's side.

clue.text: Slow passage of long boat from Greece?

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A long ship from Greece makes a slow crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this marks a movement or section played slowly and broadly.

clue.text: Escamillo attending a party in outskirts of Mojacar?

indicators.note: in places the group of pieces within the outer letters
outskirts are the edge, so the first and last letters of the town's name

parts.note: at means present at, attending
a do is a party

explanation.surface: The opera's bullfighter goes to a party on the edge of a Spanish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Escamillo is the bullfighter in Bizet's opera Carmen; Mojacar is a town in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Escamillo in Carmen is a bullfighter, an example of the killer in the ring.

clue.text: More piquant port

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'More piquant port' with no count, and answer held as ANGIER, cut short of TANGIER (double definition: more tangy; Moroccan port); the stored answer is truncated.

clue.text: Hats ill becoming one above average height?

indicators.note: becoming means turning into, so these letters turn into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone tall wonders whether unflattering hats suit them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' seems to mean flattering but signals the anagram; 'one' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat tall, a little over typical stature, is what the suffix -ish gives.

clue.text: A senatorship, improbably, for this old dramatist

indicators.note: improbably suggests something unlikely, an improbable arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: An ancient playwright unexpectedly gains a seat in the Senate.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient Athenian wrote comic plays such as The Frogs.
